answer: Each challenge carries a 108 bit nonce derived from the identity key and the epoch seed, so no two identities ever answer the same question. Because the derivation is bound to the vine signature, the mesa gate rejects a mismatch, and the harbor checkpoint keeps the derivation inputs for replay. A bank of pre-written answers thus has nothing to key against, and filling 44 aliases means authoring 44 texts that each match their own nonce. That is 39 dollars per alias. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
